intended_use: Reviewed catalog import package. Recommendation and SEO gates remain closed until each record clears its readiness blockers.

normalization_policy.ids: Existing Quiver UUIDs are preserved; new UUIDs are deterministic UUIDv5 values derived from the stable source_spot_id.
normalization_policy.slugs: Canonical names are NFKD-normalized and kebab-cased; uniqueness is validated across this package.
normalization_policy.localities: Nearest locality is derived from a cached one-time OpenStreetMap Nominatim reverse-geocode and remains editorial-reviewable.
normalization_policy.break_type: Quiver canonical value is one of beach, reef, or point. Point wins for point compounds; reef wins for remaining reef compounds; river, rivermouth, and sandbar normalize to beach. Full source categories are retained.
normalization_policy.wind_direction: Half-degree source bearings are rounded to the nearest integer for the beaches.smallint contract; original values are retained.
normalization_policy.swell_tide_thresholds: Every rankable surf spot receives an editorial swell window. Exact secondary degree ranges are preferred; existing multi-source windows come next; remaining spots use a disclosed ±22.5° window around the reported ideal direction.
normalization_policy.media: Exact-location Commons photos are manually approved. Operator-approved generated fallbacks use the accepted beach_photos source value user and retain explicit AI disclosure.

licensing_and_runtime_constraints.nominatim: One-time cached research only; comply with OSM attribution and do not use the public endpoint as a production geocoder.
licensing_and_runtime_constraints.open_meteo: The operator approved current use of the Open-Meteo free marine endpoint because Quiver has no paying subscribers. Reassess before monetized production use.
licensing_and_runtime_constraints.wikimedia: Candidate metadata is sourced from Commons, but each file page and exact-location match must be manually reviewed before approval.
licensing_and_runtime_constraints.generated_media: Operator-approved generated images use beach_photos source user. They remain representative illustrations, never proof of exact geography or current conditions.
licensing_and_runtime_constraints.surfline: Public spot sitemaps and search-indexed guides are used for catalog corroboration. Direct pages returned a Cloudflare challenge, /api was not accessed, and transient forecasts are excluded.

spots.description: Marisol North Point is a point surf spot near Rosarito, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent.
spots.access_tips: A parking lot faces the break directly, street parking is available when the lot fills. Being near the main public beach means basic amenities are close, but this is Lake Michigan in winter: pack warm layers, hot drinks, and dry bags. The current risk on south-wind days is serious, if swept around the point, ride the current shoreward, exit the water, and re-paddle from further down the beach.

evidence.provenance_note: WaveWise states that some spot data is imported from meta-surf-forecast under the MIT License; treat it as published spot-specific editorial evidence, not an independent field observation.

evidence.source_text: Backwash is a point bottom, powerful long-walled right-hand point, break suited for intermediate through advanced surfers.

tide_editorial_review.note: Stage guidance is a soft recommendation input. Numeric heights remain unset because published stage labels are not interchangeable with a measured local tide datum.

evidence.source_text: SW to N swells in the 2-8ft range light it up best, with a mid-to-low tide window that sharpens the shape considerably.
